description:
JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 ('apply_space_patch MemoryBackend: Role + Member variants') is currently `human`-labeled and open. Per its 2026-05-12 notes block, the explicit reason for the label was that JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 (the Space.ownerId revert) had to land first.

JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 closed 2026-05-12T16:25:45Z — 13 minutes after JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3's most recent update at 16:12:41Z. The stated blocker is now resolved.

Question for the human:

Should JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 lose its `human` label so the autonomous /do-beads loop can pick it up?

Considerations:

  - The bead is sized at ~600-800 LOC + tests, covering permission gating, role-hierarchy enforcement, RemoveRole cascade-to-@everyone, ULID assignment, single-user-mode handling, and a new `protect_last_admin` config knob on MemoryBackend.
  - The 2026-05-12 design reversal dropped the owner-protection requirements (Space.ownerId is no longer normative), so the work is bounded by a clean acceptance block in the bead's notes. The shape feels claimable autonomously now.
  - Closing JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 also unblocks JMAP-g7wu.2.4.6 (integration tests for the 12 sub-op mutations), which is currently the only other actionable but dep-blocked work.

Recommendation: de-label `human` on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 unless there is a remaining concern (e.g., the spec direction is still unsettled, or the protect_last_admin knob shape needs a separate human sign-off).

Filed because the do-beads loop hit no autonomous ready frontier (only epics + human-labeled beads remained) and this is the highest-leverage unblock available.
title: Re-evaluate JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 human label — its blocker JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 has closed
